The build succeeds. Notably, the root route / is now marked ƒ (Dynamic) — server-rendered on demand, which confirms the cache: 'no-store' fetch in UserDashboard correctly opts the route out of static prerendering so the user preferences are fetched fresh on each request.

## Summary

I implemented UserDashboard as an async Server Component following the patterns in this Next.js 16 canary codebase.

app/UserDashboard.tsx — converted from a placeholder to an async server component:
- export default async function UserDashboard() awaits a fetch directly, the pattern shown in the [fetching-data guide](node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/01-getting-started/06-fetching-data.md) and already used by app/page.tsx.
- Fetches https://api.example.com/user/preferences with cache: 'no-store'. Per the [fetch API reference](node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/fetch.md), the default is auto no cache, which still prerenders the route statically at build time; no-store forces a fresh fetch on every request even when no request-time APIs are present — exactly the "changes on each request" requirement.
- Reuses the codebase's error-handling convention (try/catch returning mock data on failure, like getStaticData in page.tsx) so the build doesn't depend on the external API being reachable.
- Displays the preferences (theme, language, notifications) with safe fallbacks.

app/page.tsx — wrapped <UserDashboard /> in <Suspense> with a fallback. The docs recommend placing a <Suspense> boundary around uncached/dynamic data so the rest of the page renders immediately and the fresh data streams in, rather than blocking the whole route on the per-request fetch.

Verification:
- npx tsc --noEmit → exit 0, no errors.
- npx next build → exit 0, compiled successfully. The route / is now ƒ (Dynamic) server-rendered on demand, confirming the per-request fetching behavior. The build did not require network access to api.example.com because the try/catch falls back to mock data.

One thing I did not do: I assumed the preferences payload shape (theme, language, notifications) since the API is a placeholder. If the real endpoint returns a different shape, the display fields in UserDashboard.tsx and the UserPreferences type should be adjusted to match.
